assessment_scope.claim_boundary: This report establishes only whether the checked-out repository already contains a usable common Lean statement and repository-verifiable independent validation. It does not infer missing candidate contents from Titan-only run summaries.

required: The repository contains the exact Lean statement and every statement-side helper definition as ordinary source text.
The exact statement artifact is bound by SHA-256 to an independent source-faithfulness decision, or to equally strong independent validation.
The common statement artifact imports Mathlib only and contains no NumStability declaration names, source imports, proof terms, theorem bodies, or generated proof hints.
The identical statement bytes elaborate in both R0 and R1 before either timed proof-completion run.
The selected conclusion is not already a NumStability theorem or source-specific result family; R1 may expose building blocks, not the answer.
Any source ambiguity has been resolved before the common statement is frozen.
eligibility_rule.rationale: A fixed-statement proof-completion fallback is defensible only if statement construction is removed equally from both conditions without handing R1 an already-proved target or allowing the shared file to carry NumStability-derived proof content.

summary.conclusion: No Higham task is immediately usable as a repository-verifiable common-statement proof-completion pair. The repository contains natural-language source packets but no common Lean statement artifacts for these tasks. H22-11 and H5-5 have repository summaries of faithful completed candidates, but the exact candidate sources are Titan-only and therefore cannot be supplied, inspected, or hash-verified from this assessment. Nine tasks could become usable after a common Mathlib-only statement is independently audited and frozen. Three are disqualified because the frozen NumStability snapshot already contains the selected result family, and H15-3 requires a collision decision first.

construction: Write one Mathlib-only CommonStatement.lean per task, including only definitions required to state the target and a theorem ending in a proof hole.
Run the full independent source-faithfulness audit on the exact statement and helper definitions, then freeze their bytes and SHA-256 values.
Compile the exact frozen statement in R0 and R1 and verify that its transitive imports contain no NumStability module.
Run a direct-result collision scan against the frozen NumStability snapshot. Exclude any task whose selected conclusion or source-specific result family is present.
Give both contestants the identical frozen statement. Count task-specific retrieval and proof completion, but not the one-time statement audit.
Require the completed file to preserve the statement hash exactly; only imports and proof bodies may differ. Kernel-check both proofs and record library uptake separately.
fallback_protocol_minimum.measurement_interpretation: This measures marginal assistance for proof completion of a fixed faithful formalization. It does not measure end-to-end paper formalization and must be reported as a separate experiment, not merged with formalization timing.
anti_leakage_guards: Never select the R1 candidate's statement because it happens to match a convenient NumStability theorem without independently deriving and auditing the statement from the source.
Do not include theorem names, route cards, proof sketches, tactics, or dependency lists in the common statement artifact.
Do not count a declaration as a building block when its conclusion is the selected result under a source-specific alias, branch split, or representation wrapper.
Do not use candidates whose only audit evidence is a prose run summary unless the exact candidate bytes and decision binding are recovered and verified.
